requirements.requirement: Run the repaired collector on node1 UDP/9098 and append valid node2 datagrams in meter_id,sequence,reading format.
requirements.summary: Node2 sent valid datagrams to node1; node1 appended west,2,43 and east,1,11, remained active and listening, and continued receiving traffic after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Ignore duplicate meter/sequence pairs, including after collector restarts.
requirements.summary: A duplicate west,2 datagram appeared only once. After an observed collector PID change, conflicting duplicates for west,1 and west,2 left readings.csv unchanged. Duplicate suppression also remained effective after node reboots.

requirements.requirement: Record malformed datagrams separately without terminating collection, and accept only nonnegative decimal sequence and reading fields.
requirements.summary: The repaired code directly validates ASCII decimal fields. A malformed datagram was written to malformed.log and excluded from readings.csv, while a subsequent valid datagram was ingested and the service remained active. This behavior was repeated successfully after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the previously recorded reading under /srv/legacy2/udp-meter-ingestion, including across collector restarts.
requirements.summary: The seeded west,1,42 record was observed before modification, retained exactly once across a collector-process restart, resisted a conflicting duplicate, and was recovered unchanged after node1 reboot. Node2's seeded local files also retained their original checksums after its reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 before and after execution. The Python collector ran successfully under the installed Python 3 environment and recovered after reboot; package-health observations remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both managed nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity corroborated by fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered service/network/data state. Collection behavior was revalidated after both restarts.
limitations: Behavioral tests covered representative valid, duplicate, malformed, post-malformed, restart, and reboot cases rather than every possible payload boundary; the supplied collector source provides the remaining validation evidence.

Fixed lifecycle snapshots do not inventory application data, so application-level recovery relies on the detailed executor commands; their boot identities agree with the independent lifecycle observations.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1, seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The retained backup, dedicated account, data permissions, repaired collector, systemd unit, and source-scoped firewall rule all had clear implementation or rollback roles. Test datagrams were bounded functional evidence. The syntax check created __pycache__ state, which was explicitly removed before final evidence. Reboots served the mandatory provider protocol. Final observations showed no failed services, healthy package state, no abandoned temporary work file, and only the intended UDP/9098 listener added on node1.
